| [0021](0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) | Live test/demo-data environment (retail model, 3 reference flows) lives outside the repo — IaC stack/mock-data/Databricks notebook not git-tracked; discharges the deferred live-warehouse/file smoke | Accepted (amended 2026-07-27 — harness IaC CLI is **OpenTofu**, converted with the app stack; see ADR 0024) |
| [0022](0022-week6-prototype-adoption-and-chart-library.md) | Week-6 prototype adoption — full 13-screen set as dedicated pages (Share is the only drawer; prototype wins on conflicts; Settings/Admin pulled into W6); chart library = recharts (lazy-loaded) | Accepted |
| [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) | Container image registry — GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) over ACR / Docker Hub (vendor-neutral, public package → anonymous ACA pull, reuses `GITHUB_TOKEN`); supersedes the earlier ACR scaffolding | Accepted |
| [0024](0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md) | App deploy infra — in-repo IaC stack; shares subscription/RG/ACA-env/Postgres with the harness; ACA api+worker+migrate-job + SWA-Standard linked same-origin `/api` + self-hosted Redis + KV (UAMI) + App Insights + AAD-app-reg OIDC | Accepted (amended 2026-07-27 — **OpenTofu** replaces Terraform as the IaC CLI, in-place amendment; ADR 0031 coherence, state/providers/path unchanged) |
| [0025](0025-production-image-pip-slim.md) | Production image — multi-stage `python:3.13-slim` + pip (not conda; ~2.84GB→~1GB); conda stays the local-dev tool; amends the W1 conda lock | Accepted |
| [0026](0026-auth-api-keys-and-principal-seam.md) | DataQ-issued API keys (PATs) as a second authenticator behind the `get_current_user` seam — REST + `/mcp` identically; phase 1 = user-scoped PATs (`dq_live_…`, sha256-at-rest, show-once, uniform 401, mandatory expiry, owner-cascade); service-account principals = phase 2 (deferred); HTTP Basic rejected | Accepted (phase 1 built 2026-07-04; amended by 0032 — email-identity slice of the phase-2 principal question) |
| [0027](0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) | Suite permissions — workspace-admin is implicit `admin` on every suite (governance/break-glass); drop grantable suite-admin; normal users get owner/edit/view; workspace-admin gets workspace-wide visibility (supersedes earlier, narrower workspace-admin decisions) | Accepted (amended by 0033 — admin source → stored `users.role`; Viewer share-cap) |
| [0028](0028-cloud-neutral-image-runtime-config-generic-oidc.md) | Cloud-neutral image — one multi-arch frontend image, nothing baked; auth config injected at runtime (`window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` via nginx envsubst) behind a generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract; bypass fail-closed (explicit `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` only); replace MSAL with a generic OIDC client validated against Azure; frontend SWA→Container App (amends 0024); AWS/GCP IaC post-v1 | Accepted (amended by 0032 — `otp` mode + cookie session credential) |
| [0029](0029-dbt-orchestration-provider.md) | dbt as a **third** `OrchestrationProvider` (mirrors the Airflow callback model 0007) — HMAC webhook + artifacts poll of `run_results.json` (adls/s3/file); binds to dbt's universal surface (no host API); job-level grain; migration widens the connection-type/provider/dedup value-sets | Accepted |
| [0030](0030-iceberg-native-read-path.md) | Apache Iceberg — engine-level read (Snowflake/UC iceberg tables) is free & zero-code; the only new build is a **native `pyiceberg` read** (v2 baseline, v3 deferred) behind a thin `IcebergCheckRunner` (scan → DataFrame → `gx_runner`); new **self-contained** `iceberg` connection type (Option A: own catalog + storage credential — independent lifecycle, cascade-safe), Option B two-connection ref deferred to 0015; reads Delta UniForm too; native impl deferred | Accepted (native read shipped; introspection built) |
| [0031](0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md) | Distribution licensing — **free open-source (MIT) + customer-deployed BYOL**; no entitlement/license-key (amends 0013: supersedes its §5 licensing-model line + licensed-revenue framing); marketplace listings are free offers of the OSS artifacts; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES/SBOM in images + releases; standing no-strong-copyleft dependency guardrail (CONTRIBUTING rule 40) | Accepted |
| [0032](0032-email-otp-signin.md) | Email OTP sign-in — passwordless **third authenticator** behind `get_current_user` (`dq_sess_` cookie sessions, PAT-style sha256-at-rest); auth-mode ladder `bypass · otp · oidc`, fail-closed startup; mandatory signup allowlist (no open registration); one user row per normalized email (aad_object_id → nullable, two-step); separate `AUTH_EMAIL_*` mailer + SMTP pre-flight; hard prereq = the rate-limiting auth slice; amends 0026 (email-identity slice) + 0028 (mode enum + cookie credential) | Accepted (amended by 0033 — signup default role + widened trust statement) |
| [0033](0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md) | Workspace roles — **Admin / Member / Viewer** as stored `users.role` on the two-axis model (role × per-suite ladder, ladder untouched); **connection mutations Admin-only** (closes the workspace-global hole, breaking for Members); Viewer capped at `view`; `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` demotes to bootstrap/break-glass; in-app role management + last-admin guard; amends 0027 (admin source) + 0032 (signup default role) | Accepted |
| [0034](0034-asset-entity-openlineage-identity-lineage-pull.md) | Assets & lineage (gap G-d design) — first-class **asset entity keyed by the OpenLineage dataset-naming spec** (namespace+name adopted verbatim, dbt-ol/Spark byte-compatible; DEV/QA = distinct assets, UI groups over `env`); **lineage emitted/pulled, never built** — OL emission w/ quality facets → dbt `manifest.json` → `lineage_edges` cache → `LineageProvider` seam (Marquez reference; OpenMetadata SDK license-blocked per 0031); incidents anchor to assets (one open per asset+check, evidence-card payload); asset/incident authz derived from suite grants. *Amended 2026-09-27:* column grain stays a refinement on the table edge with a per-edge `column_coverage` reason; Snowflake column pairs come from `ACCESS_HISTORY` on every tier; placement/dedup advisory, classification propagation additive-only | Accepted |
| [0035](0035-request-rate-limiting.md) | Request rate limiting — **app-level innermost HTTP middleware** (portable per 0028/0013, covers the `/mcp` mount a dependency can't, principal-aware where nginx isn't); fixed-window Redis counter (window index in the key → no EXPIRE race), **no new dep** (INCR over slowapi/limits); **fail-open**; endpoint classes `webhook`(per-IP) · `default`(per-`sha256(token)`) · `unauth`(per-IP), raw token never keyed/logged; `/healthz`+`OPTIONS` exempt; headers on 429 only; nginx `limit_req` out of scope; hard prereq for 0032's OTP | Accepted |
| [0036](0036-connection-anchored-check-engines.md) | Connection-anchored check engines — **engines are capabilities of connections** (GX universal; `dmf`⇔snowflake, `dqx`⇔unity_catalog, `dataplex`⇔future bigquery); **`check.engine`** per check (supersedes 0003's suite-level `gx \| dqx` toggle); type gates the offer, connection **probe** validates reality (classified remediation, never raw errors); **`kind` ⊥ `engine`** (engines = alternate evaluators of existing kinds; engine-aware backend catalog lands with the dimension-classification work); lifecycle validated save/run/import-time (`error` status, never silent); DMF first build (custom DMFs added by the 2026-09-29 amendment), DQX shipped 2026-09-28 (remote execution), Dataplex trigger-gated; scheduled-native ingest deferred to a future ADR | Accepted (amends 0003; DMF incl. custom DMFs and DQX shipped, DQX stream mode 2026-09-29; Dataplex trigger-gated) |
| [0037](0037-workspace-visible-asset-identity.md) | Workspace-visible asset identity — **asset identity + lineage topology (incl. column pairs) visible to every member**; aggregate verdicts (health rollup, future scorecard) **workspace-true** (all composing suites, one number for all viewers); grant boundary moves to **suite-derived detail** (composing-suite names/runs/results/samples/incidents — ADR 0027 ladder unchanged, suite-grain 404-no-leak intact); asset detail 200s for all, `restricted_suite_count` replaces redaction; supersedes an earlier identity-redaction regime (amends 0034 decision 5) | Accepted |
| [0038](0038-dq-dimension-classification.md) | DQ-dimension classification on checks — **seven canonical dimensions** (accuracy/completeness/consistency/integrity/timeliness/uniqueness/validity) as a **closed** vocabulary via table `CHECK`, not a Postgres ENUM (no `ALTER TYPE` friction) and not free text (unbounded values destroy coverage reporting); **derived default → stored → overridable at any time** (stored so the scorecard aggregates in SQL and an override survives); derivation is **deliberately partial** — `accuracy`/`integrity` are never derived and custom SQL has no answer, so **NULL means unclassified** and the scorecard must render it as a gap; **existing rows ARE backfilled** (migration `a7b8c9d0e1f2`; §5 **amended 2026-07-19** — the backfill cannot overwrite a human decision because none existed yet when it ran, while leaving them NULL made the scorecard useless on day one; unmapped types stay NULL); `dimension` ⊥ `kind` ⊥ `engine`; narrows 0036 §4 — lands the derivation map as the backend catalog's seed without moving the frontend catalog server-side, since no native engine exists yet | Accepted |
| [0039](0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md) | Self-hosted secret backend — a fourth `SecretStore` speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API, not a vendor SDK** (one mode serves OpenBao / Vault Community / Enterprise / HCP; no HashiCorp lock-in traded for the Azure one); **OpenBao** (MPL-2.0, LF fork of pre-BUSL Vault 1.14) is the shipped/tested/pinned server — Vault Community is BUSL-1.1 and rule-40-forbidden as a *distributed* component, supported as a *target*; **`SECRET_STORE=openbao` replaces `redis` and `RedisSecretStore` is deleted** (plaintext credentials were the default of the published eval stack), with a loud one-cycle `RuntimeError` shim, **Redis stays** for broker + rate-limit counters; token auth phase 1 (AppRole deferred/filed), dev-mode token generated into the gitignored `.env`; Azure Key Vault remains the prod default (managed identity beats a held token), OpenBao is the BYOL/cloud-neutral option; **an outage is never reportable as a state** — new `SecretStoreUnavailableError`, deliberately NOT a `SecretNotFoundError` subclass, since every caller branches on the TYPE and none reads the message (a sealed vault otherwise renders "not set" on the admin page, skips alert delivery silently, and runs connections with the credential omitted); no status is silent (400=KV v1 mount, 401=gateway, 429=HCP throttle); **`AzureKeyVaultStore` had the same defect since Week 2** and is fixed too (the same invisible-degradation shape seen before); `delete` purges via KV v2 **metadata** delete, fail-soft | Accepted |
| [0040](0040-warehouse-inventory-sync-table-enumeration-seam.md) | Warehouse inventory sync + the **table-enumeration seam** — one per-datasource `enumerate_tables` capability (Snowflake/UC `information_schema`, engine-native case = the identity-safe path, connection-database scoping, ephemera/system schemas excluded) feeding three consumers: **inventory sync** (opt-in per connection, daily crontab beat, `upsert_assets(preserve_provenance=True)` so `last_seen` advancement keeps live tables out of the orphan sweep and dropped tables age out through it — no new column, no new guard; no "discovered" badge, ADR 0037's neutral unmonitored rendering IS the marker), **GET_LINEAGE seeds**, and future pickers; `ASSET_INVENTORY_MAX_TABLES` cap (default 2000) with loud truncation; **decided**: S3 namespace stays `s3://{bucket}` for AWS, becomes `s3://{host[:port]}/{bucket}` only when `endpoint_url` is set | Accepted |
| [0041](0041-history-audit-strategy.md) | History & audit posture for v1.x+ (amends 0020) — **one append-only `audit_events` table** (actor/action/entity/before/after/ts) recording **deliberate acts by a principal only**, with `entity_id` deliberately **FK-less** so the row outlives the entity it describes (an FK would either cascade the audit away or block the delete); the data-**read** audit (gap G1) is **phase 2 on the same table**, discriminated by `action_class` — not a second table — with the opposite latency contract (phase 1 writes inside the mutation's transaction, fail-closed; phase-2 reads must stay off the critical path); **(a) preserving `check_versions` past delete rejected** — `RESTRICT` makes checks undeletable, `SET NULL` orphans rows needing self-contained identity (a worse audit log scoped to one entity), tombstone = soft-delete for one table — the audit log's delete event answers it instead and **cascade stands**; **(b) soft-delete re-deferred** on a narrowed argument (its headline motivation is already met — an earlier 409 guard means a connection can no longer be deleted out from under its runs; the column is the easy part vs. "deleted means inert" for live credentials/bindings/schedules; and a delete-that-doesn't-delete fights the G2 Art-17 erasure work), mitigated by a follow-up blast-radius confirmation; **(d) SCD-2 closed permanently**, not deferred; Type-4 tables stay the **product** surface (version drawer/restore), the audit log is the **durable record**; payloads are **per-entity allow-lists** reusing the snapshot builders, never `dict(row)`, never a secret value, never `sample_failures`/`observed_value`, and reuse only the **credential subset** of `_PII_KEYS` (the full set redacts `name`/`display_name`/`user_id` — the very content of a rename and the point of the actor record); append-only via `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` — **a guard against accidental in-app mutation, explicitly NOT tamper-resistance** (`dataq_app` owns the table and can re-grant; splitting the role is rejected because the single-role model is the whole mitigation for the unpatched Postgres RI owner-cast escalation, so real tamper-evidence needs the G1 external anchor); coverage guarded off FastAPI's **route table**, not an audit registry (the ADR-0039 tautology) | Accepted (phase-1 build; follow-ups filed; amended 2026-10-20 — the second `TamperAnchor` class, S3 Object Lock / Azure immutable blob, with read-back verification) |
| [0042](0042-llm-provider-seam.md) | `LLMProvider` seam — outbound LLM for authoring assistance (NL→SQL generation, check suggestions, future RCA narrative), **admin-configured, BYO credential, default-OFF**; two wire impls only (`anthropic` official SDK + `openai_compatible` httpx — the latter covers Azure OpenAI, Bedrock chat-completions, and local Ollama/vLLM/TGI; no model server in the image per 0025); structured output is a `native \| prompt_json` capability ladder and **never a trust boundary** — callers re-validate, generated SQL rides the 0019 validator + dry-run, suggestions the server-side allowlist; config = `llm_settings` DB singleton behind `require_workspace_admin`, API key write-only in `SecretStore` with the credential-destination re-supply rule on `base_url`; execution worker-side through `llm_invocations` (poll + audit + token/cost record; G4 posture reads it); prompt context = schema + masked aggregate profiler stats only, never sample rows; rejected: proxying a vendor key we own, bundling weights, MCP exposure, per-feature providers | Accepted |
| [0043](0043-in-app-workspace-membership.md) | In-app workspace membership — one `workspace_members` table an admin manages from Admin → Members; **empty table = today's behaviour, non-empty = member if in the env allowlist OR the table**, checked on every request at four points (`_upsert_user`, OTP session resolve, PAT resolve, OTP eligibility) so removing someone stops their browser session and their PATs on the next request; env allowlists become a starting seed plus an emergency way in that can only grant (OTP mode still needs a non-empty one to boot); the first row imports every existing user as a **provisional** member shown for review, never a silent backfill; last-admin removal refused, self-removal confirmed; `initial_role` applies only when the user row is first created; the IdP account stays a prerequisite — DataQ controls its own door only; REST denies with 403, `/mcp` with 401 | Accepted |
| [0044](0044-mssql-tds-driver-and-entra-auth.md) | MSSQL / T-SQL adapter driver + auth — **`python-tds` + `sqlalchemy-pytds` (MIT, pure Python, FEDAUTH token) by default** for SQL Server / Azure SQL / Synapse, with the adapter shipping its own SAN hostname validator and named-instance routing fix (both driver defects found in the live spike); **Fabric SQL endpoints via an optional ODBC lane** (`mssql+pyodbc` when the operator installs msodbcsql18 — never redistributed by DataQ) because python-tds's routed login to Fabric fails; one engine-generic `mssql` type with `sql` / `entra_service_principal` auth, `destination_fields` host/port/tenant_id/auth_type | Accepted |
| [0045](0045-engine-generic-sql-datasource-base.md) | Engine-generic SQL datasource base — one config/adapter/runner/enumerator parameterized by a **`SqlEngineSpec`** (driver, GX datasource factory, `connect_args`, namespace scheme, catalog queries, optional profiler and run-engine hooks), one registry every SQL capability set derives from; **pushdown only** (no sampling), **read-only sessions** at the server, names resolved **exactly as spelled** (GX session scoped to the target schema, never a lower-cased GX schema), identifier limits enforced at save time; honest gaps — no column-tag source, no warehouse-native lineage (enumeration only, via a separate `TableEnumerator` seam), GX engine only; PostgreSQL first, then MySQL/MariaDB (amendment: `temp_table_types` — GX's MySQL uniqueness check runs on its own non-read-only session; `url_database`), then Trino (amendment: `auth_connect_args` — auth object, secret never in the URL; `requires_secret` for auth `none`; JWT `credential_expiry`; per-spec `destination_fields`; `names_are_lower_case` — and **no read-only session** on Trino, where the credential's access control is the guarantee), then SQL Server, then Amazon Athena (amendment: host derived from the region, `url_query`, `namespace_includes_port`, an IAM policy as the read-only guarantee, and a GX regex branch for the pyathena dialect), then Amazon Redshift (amendment: read-only like PostgreSQL; `gx_schema_with_session` for GX's name-only column lookup, `columns_view` for late-binding views, `namespace_authority` for OpenLineage's `<cluster>.<region>`), then Google BigQuery (amendment: `url_host`/`url_port`, a client connect arg carrying a per-query `maximum_bytes_billed` cap, `SqlCatalog.api` for the free metadata API, `namespace_override` for the bare `bigquery` namespace; IAM roles as the read-only guarantee) | Accepted |
| [0046](0046-pipeline-dq-gate.md) | Pipeline DQ gate — a fourth orchestration responsibility: **answer a gate request**. One provider-agnostic endpoint (`POST /orchestration/gate`) keyed by trigger bindings: **trigger-and-wait** (starts the bound suites' runs for this pipeline run under the success-event marker, so polls and the later success event are idempotent; needs `edit`) or **status only** (`view`); states `awaiting_trigger` · `running` · `passed` · `failed` (at/above `fail_on`) · `error`; a bound suite the caller can't see refuses the gate; clients are the `dataq gate` CLI, an Airflow sensor and an ADF Until-loop snippet, all fail-closed; DataQ still never mutates a pipeline | Accepted |
| [0047](0047-automated-coverage-loop.md) | Automated coverage — **per-connection switch** (`auto_coverage`, enumerable warehouse types only, per-asset exclusion) turns every inventory table into a **system-owned suite** (`suites.origin = 'auto'`, one per asset) of ordinary checks, so runs, results, incidents, alerts, UI and MCP need nothing new; **universal baselines start without approval** (row-count and freshness anomaly, schema drift, and a new one-query `column_profile` anomaly metric over every column's null % and distinct count), while **rules that assert something** (not-null, unique, accepted values, ranges, from profiling or the LLM suggester) wait in a `check_suggestions` review queue; **full severity** (warn 3σ, fail 4σ, critical 6σ; schema change fails); the reconciler adds missing checks only and never overrides a person's edit or resurrects a deleted check; daily staggered schedules and `AUTO_COVERAGE_MAX_ASSETS` bound the warehouse cost; incident `resolution` makes the **false-positive rate** a tracked figure beside coverage; **amended 2026-10-13:** sensitivity (per baseline) and baseline shape are settings resolved **asset override → workspace setting → built-in default**, and automatic anomaly checks **inherit them at run time** until a person edits one | Accepted |
| [0048](0048-per-period-metrics-yearly-seasonality.md) | Per-period metrics and yearly seasonality on the anomaly monitor — two **per-period metrics** (`period_row_count`, `period_sum`, bucketed by a date column, complete UTC periods only, observations keyed by period); history **seeded once from the table** (marked `backfilled`) and then **accumulated from runs** (`observed`); **yearly seasonality as a seasonal index** over the rolling baseline, on every single-number anomaly metric (and, as a default-off switch, on the automatic row-count and freshness baselines), with every input in the result and an index of 1 when no earlier year exists; **seasonal periods** declared in a workspace calendar that a check attaches to, and detected from history for display only; the per-period metrics are authored checks, not automatic coverage | Accepted |
| [0049](0049-profiler-pii-classification-source.md) | Profiler-detected PII as a classification source — one `asset_column_classifications` table (`source = 'profiler'` now, the catalog pull next) holding **additive-only** `sensitive` verdicts from the two existing value detectors (email, encoded), overlaid on `effective_column_tags` as `detected`: a warehouse tag, inherited `sensitive` and the suite's `pii_columns` outrank it, the suite's `identifier_column` clears it, it never satisfies fail-closed clearance and never travels along lineage; cleared only by an audited Admin dismissal that survives re-detection; written on every profile of the suite's own target | Accepted |
| [0050](0050-usage-telemetry.md) | Opt-in product-usage telemetry — **OpenTelemetry signals** through the existing exporter seam: one `dataq.usage.events` counter (attribute `event`) and one `dataq.usage.<event>` log event per occurrence, on a `MeterProvider`/`LoggerProvider` of their own; **default OFF behind two gates**, the operator's `TELEMETRY_SINK` (`off` · `file` JSON lines · `otlp`) and the admin's audited opt-in (`telemetry_settings` singleton, Admin → Settings); a **closed, code-enforced vocabulary** of twelve events whose attributes are counts or fixed value sets (never a table/column name, SQL, suite name, email or free text — a value outside its set is dropped); the browser posts only `page_viewed`/`check_editor_abandoned` to the server, which is the only emitter; disclosed in `GET /admin/deployment` in both states; no third-party analytics dependency | Accepted |
| [0051](0051-suite-on-suite-triggers.md) | Suite-on-suite triggers — a suite's own success as a **trigger provider** (`provider='suite'`, `pipeline_or_dag_id` = the upstream suite's id, env derived from it) in the existing `trigger_bindings`, **not** an orchestration provider (no connection, poller, webhook or `pipeline_runs` row; the gate refuses it); fires from the worker after the run's terminal commit when the run `succeeded` with no check at fail/critical; marker `suite:<suite>:<run>` under the same dedup index; self-binding and cycles refused at authoring (disabled bindings count), chain depth capped at 5 at firing, `view` on the upstream suite required | Accepted |

1	"""Telemetry and lineage leave the backend only through their open-standard seams (rule 45)."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import ast
6	import functools
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	_APP = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "app"
10	
11	_OTEL_SEAM = {
12	    "core/otel.py",
13	    "core/tracing.py",
14	    "core/logging.py",
15	    "core/usage_telemetry.py",
16	}
17	_EXPORTER_SEAM = {"core/otel.py"}
18	_EXPORTER_PACKAGES = ("opentelemetry.exporter", "azure.monitor")
19	_LINEAGE_SEAM_DIR = "lineage/"
20	_PROPRIETARY_TELEMETRY = (
21	    "opencensus",
22	    "applicationinsights",
23	    "ddtrace",
24	    "datadog",
25	    "newrelic",
26	    "sentry_sdk",
27	    "prometheus_client",
28	    "statsd",
29	    "elasticapm",
30	    "logfire",
31	    "rollbar",
32	    "bugsnag",
33	    "honeybadger",
34	    "aws_xray_sdk",
35	    "google.cloud.trace",
36	    "google.cloud.logging",
37	    "instana",
38	    "dynatrace",
39	    "splunk_otel",
40	    "scout_apm",
41	    "appdynamics",
42	)
43	_DYNAMIC_IMPORTERS = {"import_module", "__import__"}
44	
45	
46	def _dynamic_import(node: ast.Call) -> str | None:
47	    func = node.func
48	    name = func.attr if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) else getattr(func, "id", None)
49	    if name not in _DYNAMIC_IMPORTERS or not node.args:
50	        return None
51	    first = node.args[0]
52	    return first.value if isinstance(first, ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value, str) else None
53	
54	
55	@functools.cache
56	def _imports() -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
57	    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
58	    for path in _APP.rglob("*.py"):
59	        rel = path.relative_to(_APP).as_posix()
60	        for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
61	            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
62	                found.append((rel, node.module))
63	            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
64	                found.extend((rel, alias.name) for alias in node.names)
65	            elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and (module := _dynamic_import(node)):
66	                found.append((rel, module))
67	    return tuple(found)
68	
69	
70	def _offenders(prefix: str, allowed: set[str] | None = None, allowed_dir: str = "") -> set[str]:
71	    return {
72	        rel
73	        for rel, module in _imports()
74	        if (module == prefix or module.startswith(prefix + "."))
75	        and rel not in (allowed or set())
76	        and not (allowed_dir and rel.startswith(allowed_dir))
77	    }
78	
79	
80	def test_opentelemetry_is_imported_only_by_the_telemetry_seam() -> None:
81	    assert _offenders("opentelemetry", _OTEL_SEAM) == set()
82	
83	
84	def test_every_exporter_is_imported_only_by_the_exporter_seam() -> None:
85	    assert set().union(*(_offenders(p, _EXPORTER_SEAM) for p in _EXPORTER_PACKAGES)) == set()
86	
87	
88	def test_no_proprietary_telemetry_sdk_is_imported() -> None:
89	    assert set().union(*(_offenders(name) for name in _PROPRIETARY_TELEMETRY)) == set()
90	
91	
92	def test_openlineage_is_imported_only_by_the_lineage_package() -> None:
93	    assert _offenders("openlineage", allowed_dir=_LINEAGE_SEAM_DIR) == set()
94	
95	
96	def test_the_scan_sees_the_seams_it_guards() -> None:
97	    modules = {module for _, module in _imports()}
98	    assert any(m.startswith("opentelemetry.exporter") for m in modules)
99	    assert any(m.startswith("openlineage") for m in modules)
100	
101	
102	def test_a_dynamic_import_is_seen() -> None:
103	    call = ast.parse("importlib.import_module('sentry_sdk')").body[0].value  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
104	    assert _dynamic_import(call) == "sentry_sdk"
105	    call = ast.parse("__import__('ddtrace')").body[0].value  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
106	    assert _dynamic_import(call) == "ddtrace"

1	# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
2	
3	Each ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
4	
5	## Format
6	
7	- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)
8	- Frontmatter fields:
9	  - **Status** — one of `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Deprecated`, `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` (title-case)
10	  - **Date** — `YYYY-MM-DD`
11	  - **Deciders** — who made the call
12	  - **Consulted** *(optional)* — stakeholders whose sign-off the decision needed (e.g. product owner for ADR 0005). Omit when none.
13	  - **Supersedes** *(optional)* — `ADR-NNNN` this decision replaces. Omit when none.
14	  - **Superseded by** *(optional)* — `ADR-NNNN` that later replaced this one. Add when the status flips to `Superseded by`.
15	  - **Amends** *(optional)* — `ADR-NNNN` this decision partially overrides (whole-ADR replacement uses `Supersedes` instead). Pair it with an inline `> **Amendment (date, ADR-NNNN):** …` blockquote at the top of the amended ADR and an "(amended by NNNN — …)" note on its index Status, so the override is visible where readers actually look. Precedents: ADR 0028 (amends 0024), ADR 0012's amendment blockquote, ADR 0031 (amends 0013).
16	- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)
17	- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.
18	
19	### Template
20	
21	```markdown
22	# ADR NNNN — <title>
23	
24	- **Status:** Proposed
25	- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
26	- **Deciders:** @handle
27	- **Consulted:** <stakeholder>   <!-- optional; omit when none -->
28	- **Supersedes:** ADR-NNNN       <!-- optional; omit when none -->
29	- **Superseded by:** ADR-NNNN    <!-- optional; add when superseded -->
30	
31	## Context
32	
33	## Decision
34	
35	## Consequences
36	
37	## Alternatives considered
38	```
39	
40	## Index
41	
42	| # | Title | Status |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| [0001](0001-trunk-based-branching.md) | Trunk-based branching with squash-merge into `main` | Accepted |
45	| [0002](0002-conventional-commits.md) | Conventional commits for PR titles and commit messages | Accepted |
46	| [0003](0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) | GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 for DLT/streaming | Accepted (amended by 0036 — suite-level `engine: gx \| dqx` toggle → check-level, connection-anchored) |
47	| [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) | Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Airflow | Accepted |
48	| [0005](0005-severity-tier-weights.md) | Severity tier weights (warn / fail / critical → health score) | Accepted (amended 2026-09-06 — the weights are a workspace setting) |
49	| [0006](0006-adf-webhook-authentication.md) | ADF webhook authentication (shared secret in URL + hard-cutover rotation) | Accepted |
50	| [0007](0007-airflow-callback-model.md) | Airflow callback model (HMAC-signed webhook + polling fallback) | Accepted |
51	| [0008](0008-mcp-server.md) | FastMCP server at `/mcp` — Azure AD token validated (same token as REST); everything exposed as tools rather than resources; thin wrappers reusing the service layer + per-suite authz; fail-closed without auth. **Amended:** 8 → 19 tools (Tier 1 reads), then 19 → 30 tools (Tier 2 edit-gated mutations + live-probe tools), then 30 → 33 → 38 (Tier 3A coherence), then 38 → 42 (Tier 3B batch 1 — assets + incidents reads) → 46 (Tier 3B batch 2 — incident lifecycle, `list_columns`, near-misses; Tier 3B complete) → 47 (`get_pipeline_status`, `get_adf_pipeline_status` kept as a deprecated alias) → 48 (`get_doc`, curated docs pages) → 51 (the reusable-notification-channel reads, `trace_column_lineage`) → 52 (`browse_connection`, run-target browsing) → 54 (`get_coverage`, `list_suggested_rules`) → **56** (`list_seasonal_periods`, `get_detected_seasonal_periods`; 32 read-only / 18 state-changing / 6 live-probe) | Accepted |
52	| [0009](0009-flat-monorepo-layout.md) | Repo layout — flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | Accepted |
53	| [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) | Provider-agnostic infrastructure seams (Azure is the default, not the architecture) | Accepted |
54	| [0011](0011-extensibility-seams-for-deferred-integrations.md) | Extensibility seams for deferred connectors and integrations | Accepted |
55	| [0012](0012-monitor-kind-seam.md) | Monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` discriminator + numeric metric storage) | Accepted |

57	| [0014](0014-reconciliation-comparison-check-kind.md) | Cross-dataset reconciliation as a `comparison` check kind (reuse FastAPI_DataComparison engine) | Accepted |
58	| [0015](0015-two-connection-comparison-check-model.md) | Two-connection comparison check model — suite stays single-connection and supplies the **target under test**; a `comparison` check adds one **source** ref (`checks.source_connection_id` FK) + suite-target-shaped `config.source`; execution via a new `DatasetReader` seam + the ported FDC engine, row-cap fail-fast; report files derived on-demand, never stored; **no** connection→connection generalization (0030 Option B stays deferred). **Amended 2026-09-16: comparison sources do not support `sampling`** — coherent key-set sampling is a different mechanism from the suite-target's positional sampling and was not built; `COMPARISON_MAX_ROWS` fail-fast + query-filter narrowing are the sanctioned alternatives | Accepted (built 2026-07-12) |

46	def _dynamic_import(node: ast.Call) -> str | None:
47	    func = node.func
48	    name = func.attr if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) else getattr(func, "id", None)
49	    if name not in _DYNAMIC_IMPORTERS or not node.args:
50	        return None
51	    first = node.args[0]
52	    return first.value if isinstance(first, ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value, str) else None

55	@functools.cache
56	def _imports() -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
57	    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
58	    for path in _APP.rglob("*.py"):
59	        rel = path.relative_to(_APP).as_posix()
60	        for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
61	            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
62	                found.append((rel, node.module))
63	            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
64	                found.extend((rel, alias.name) for alias in node.names)
65	            elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and (module := _dynamic_import(node)):
66	                found.append((rel, module))
67	    return tuple(found)

70	def _offenders(prefix: str, allowed: set[str] | None = None, allowed_dir: str = "") -> set[str]:
71	    return {
72	        rel
73	        for rel, module in _imports()
74	        if (module == prefix or module.startswith(prefix + "."))
75	        and rel not in (allowed or set())
76	        and not (allowed_dir and rel.startswith(allowed_dir))
77	    }

=================== #1977
feat: consumer-side data contract validation — contract entity + ODCS import/export
labels: enhancement,priority/P3  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
## Problem / motivation

DataQ has no first-class concept of a **data contract** — a versioned, shared spec of a table's schema + quality rules + SLA that both the team producing a dataset and the teams consuming it can validate against. Today a consumer can author ad hoc checks against a landed table, but there's no way to say "these checks exist *because* they enforce contract v3" or to trace a failure back to the specific contract clause it broke.

This issue scopes the **consumer-side half only** — validating data already at rest against a contract, using DataQ's existing GX-based check/suite execution. It's deliberately split from producer-side (pre-publish, data-in-motion) validation, which would need a separate lightweight enforcement library embedded in a producer's own pipeline — see "Out of scope" below.

## Proposed change

1. **`contracts` table** — `id`, `name`, `version`, `domain`/`owner`, `status` (draft/active/deprecated), `spec` (JSONB holding the contract document), timestamps.
2. **Suite linkage** — an optional `contract_id` + `contract_version` on `suite`, so a suite can be tagged as enforcing a specific contract without changing today's suite model (a suite with no contract works exactly as it does now).
3. **[Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS)](https://bitol-io.github.io/open-data-contract-standard/) import** — parse an ODCS YAML document into a `contracts` row, then auto-generate the corresponding checks in a linked suite: schema fields → `expectation`/`schema_drift` checks, quality rules → `expectation` checks, `slaProperties` → freshness/volume monitor-kinds. Reuses the existing `import_suite` machinery with an ODCS→DataQ-suite translation step in front of it.
4. **ODCS export** — serialize a contract (+ current suite/check state) back to ODCS YAML, mirroring `export_suite`'s shape. This is the document a future producer-side validator would consume, so both sides stay provably aligned.
5. **Traceability on violations** — when a contract-linked suite's check (particularly `schema_drift`) fails, tag the resulting incident with `contract_id` + the specific violated field/rule, so triage starts at "which clause of the contract broke" instead of a bare check name.
6. **Read surface** — REST + MCP read tools: `get_contract`, `list_contracts`, and a compliance rollup (pass/fail across a contract's linked suite(s)), following the existing asset/incident read-tool pattern (ADR 0008 Tier 1 style — read-only, no new write-gated capability needed beyond normal suite/check permissions).

## Scope

- Component(s): backend, mcp, docs
- Affected datasource(s): all (contract validation is datasource-agnostic — it rides on the existing `check`/`suite` model)
- Affected orchestration provider(s): n/a
- Schema migration required? yes — new `contracts` table + `contract_id`/`contract_version` columns on `suite` (additive, backward-compatible per the two-step migration rule)
- New external dependency? Only a YAML parsing/validation layer for ODCS documents (e.g. `pyyaml` + `jsonschema`/`pydantic`, already in the dependency tree) — no new heavy dependency, no GX-adjacent addition.

## Roadmap alignment

Net-new. Grew out of a conceptual discussion on producer/consumer data contract validation (2026-09-17) — not yet mapped to a specific cycle; candidate for `v1.2 Backlog` / `v1.3` alongside #1829, which it's related to (see below).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ODCS YAML import produces a `contracts` row + a suite with checks matching the document's schema/quality/SLA blocks
- [ ] ODCS export round-trips a contract-linked suite back to a valid ODCS document (schema-validated)
- [ ] A `schema_drift` failure on a contract-linked suite surfaces `contract_id` + violated field on the resulting incident (REST + MCP)
- [ ] `get_contract`/`list_contracts` (+ compliance rollup) exercised through the real MCP protocol, gated per ADR 0033/0027 the same as existing suite reads
- [ ] Docs: one `docs/site/` page introducing contracts, ODCS import/export, and how this differs from ADR 0014's cross-dataset `comparison` check kind (adjacent, not overlapping)

## Out of scope

- **Producer-side (pre-publish) validation** — a separate, lightweight enforcement library (e.g. a Python wheel) a producer embeds in their own write path before data lands anywhere DataQ can read it. Deferred until there's more than one producer wanting the same enforced contract; for a single producer, a stdlib-only snippet (same pattern as `integrations/airflow/`) or a synchronous call to DataQ's existing dry-run/check API is cheaper and avoids taking on a new package + release cadence for no proven multi-consumer demand. Related precedent: #1829 explicitly rejected packaging `backend/app` as an embeddable library for the same reason (no consumer asking for it yet).
- Vendoring GX Core (or any part of `backend/app`) into a separate distributable package.
- A UI contract-authoring editor (Phase 1 here is API/MCP + import/export only; a check-editor-style UI for hand-authoring a contract from scratch is a later increment if the import path proves insufficient).

## Security / observability notes

- No new auth surface: contract reads/writes ride the existing per-suite `view`/`edit` grants (ADR 0027) and workspace role (ADR 0033) — a contract without a linked suite is effectively unreachable data, so no separate permission model is needed for v1 of this.
- `contracts.spec` JSONB may contain a data owner's contact/domain metadata but no credentials or PII — no redaction requirement anticipated, but worth a pass at implementation time in case ODCS's `server`/access block ends up carrying connection-adjacent details.
- No new logging beyond the standard structlog request/task spans on the new endpoints.

The ADR for this issue should name the exact ODCS version it targets and how a newer minor is handled.

=================== #685
feat(connections): purge/redact path for connection version history (immutable snapshots retain edited-out config values)
labels: enhancement  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
Follow-up from the #683 code review (connection version-history UI, #654).

Connection version snapshots (`connection_versions`) are immutable, credential-free, and retained until the connection is deleted. `GET /connections/{id}/versions` is any-authenticated-user (consistent with the rest of the connections surface). The residual exposure, now user-visible via the #654 History drawer:

A user who mistakenly pastes a sensitive value (token, hostname-with-embedded-credential) into a **config** field — instead of the secret field — and then edits it out leaves that value readable by every authenticated workspace user indefinitely. There is no purge/redact path short of deleting the whole connection; the W5 retention sweep covers `results.sample_failures`, not connection versions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A way to remove/redact a specific connection version (or all versions), gated appropriately (owner/workspace-admin)
- [ ] Decide + document the same question for check versions (`check_versions` has the identical property)
- [ ] Test covering the purge path

Severity: low (requires user error to matter) — filed per the no-silent-deferral rule.

W7 capacity went to epic #2220 (the production-like local stack), the P2 bug batch (#1929–#1931), the health-score work (#1556–#1558) and checks-as-code phase 1 (#1688). Nothing about the issue itself changed; it is unblocked and ready to be scheduled for v1.3.

=================== #1613
RunDetail/RunReport show the check's CURRENT engine/dimension, not as-of-the-result (historical_check_context gap)
labels: enhancement  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
## What

#1551 added an engine badge to `RunDetail.tsx`'s results table and `RunReport.tsx`'s printed report, sourced from the CURRENT check (`checks.get(id)?.engine`, from `listChecks()`) — the same path `expectation_type`/`kind` already use in both surfaces. That means if a check's engine (or dimension) was changed AFTER a given result ran, both surfaces show today's value beside a historical result, not what actually evaluated it at the time.

This mirrors the caveat `run_service.historical_check_context` already exists to close for `(tested_column, expectation_type)` (#1489) — it resolves a result's check context from `check_versions` as of the result's OWN `created_at`, not the check's live state.

## Why not fixed in #1551

`historical_check_context` doesn't currently carry `engine`/`dimension` (only `column`/`expectation_type`), and `ResultRead` doesn't expose either field on the result payload — RunDetail/RunReport instead resolve them from the live `checks` map, exactly like `expectation_type`/`kind` already do. Extending the historical resolution is a small, mechanical lift now that #1489's plumbing exists, but it's server-side scope beyond a frontend badges PR, so it's deferred rather than folded in.

## Fix

- Extend `historical_check_context` (or a parallel resolver) to also return `engine` and `dimension` as of each result's `created_at`, reading from `check_versions` the same way `expectation_type` does today (note: `CheckVersion` already snapshots `engine`/`dimension` per ADR 0036/0038 restore semantics).
- Surface it on `ResultRead` (or thread it through the same per-run "context" map `runs.py`/`mcp/server.py` already build) so RunDetail/RunReport can show the AS-OF-THEN engine/dimension instead of the check's current state.
- Update RunDetail.tsx / RunReport.tsx to prefer the historical value over `checks.get(id)?.engine` once available.

## Found via

Multi-angle `/code-review` pass on PR #1551 (2026-08-28) — the altitude-angle finding recorded this as pre-existing/out-of-scope for a frontend badges PR rather than something to build inline.
--- comments:


=================== #2255
feat(privacy): a reason per entry in redacted_columns (own tag / inherited tag / policy / value classifier / default mask)
labels: enhancement,priority/P3  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
Split from #2114, which shipped the asset-level half: `inherited_classifications` on `GET /assets/{id}`, MCP `get_asset`, and a *Masked through lineage* panel on the asset page.

What remains is the per-result half. `redacted_columns` on run detail, MCP `get_run_results` and alerts says *that* a column was masked, not *why*. The decision is made per cell in `run_service._redact_row` / `_redact_comparison_row` through `_known_sensitive` / `_may_show_incidental`, which return a bool. Reporting a reason means those ladder functions return which rung decided (own tag, inherited tag, suite policy, value classifier, or the default mask for an unclassified incidental column), and `_RedactionTracker` keeps it per column.

This is a security-sensitive refactor of the redaction ladder, so it stays separate. It must not change what is masked: pin that with the existing redaction tests before touching the ladder.
--- comments:

=================== #685
feat(connections): purge/redact path for connection version history (immutable snapshots retain edited-out config values)
labels: enhancement  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
Follow-up from the #683 code review (connection version-history UI, #654).

Connection version snapshots (`connection_versions`) are immutable, credential-free, and retained until the connection is deleted. `GET /connections/{id}/versions` is any-authenticated-user (consistent with the rest of the connections surface). The residual exposure, now user-visible via the #654 History drawer:

A user who mistakenly pastes a sensitive value (token, hostname-with-embedded-credential) into a **config** field — instead of the secret field — and then edits it out leaves that value readable by every authenticated workspace user indefinitely. There is no purge/redact path short of deleting the whole connection; the W5 retention sweep covers `results.sample_failures`, not connection versions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A way to remove/redact a specific connection version (or all versions), gated appropriately (owner/workspace-admin)
- [ ] Decide + document the same question for check versions (`check_versions` has the identical property)
- [ ] Test covering the purge path

Severity: low (requires user error to matter) — filed per the no-silent-deferral rule.

=================== #1613
RunDetail/RunReport show the check's CURRENT engine/dimension, not as-of-the-result (historical_check_context gap)
labels: enhancement  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
## What

#1551 added an engine badge to `RunDetail.tsx`'s results table and `RunReport.tsx`'s printed report, sourced from the CURRENT check (`checks.get(id)?.engine`, from `listChecks()`) — the same path `expectation_type`/`kind` already use in both surfaces. That means if a check's engine (or dimension) was changed AFTER a given result ran, both surfaces show today's value beside a historical result, not what actually evaluated it at the time.

This mirrors the caveat `run_service.historical_check_context` already exists to close for `(tested_column, expectation_type)` (#1489) — it resolves a result's check context from `check_versions` as of the result's OWN `created_at`, not the check's live state.

## Why not fixed in #1551

`historical_check_context` doesn't currently carry `engine`/`dimension` (only `column`/`expectation_type`), and `ResultRead` doesn't expose either field on the result payload — RunDetail/RunReport instead resolve them from the live `checks` map, exactly like `expectation_type`/`kind` already do. Extending the historical resolution is a small, mechanical lift now that #1489's plumbing exists, but it's server-side scope beyond a frontend badges PR, so it's deferred rather than folded in.

## Fix

- Extend `historical_check_context` (or a parallel resolver) to also return `engine` and `dimension` as of each result's `created_at`, reading from `check_versions` the same way `expectation_type` does today (note: `CheckVersion` already snapshots `engine`/`dimension` per ADR 0036/0038 restore semantics).
- Surface it on `ResultRead` (or thread it through the same per-run "context" map `runs.py`/`mcp/server.py` already build) so RunDetail/RunReport can show the AS-OF-THEN engine/dimension instead of the check's current state.
- Update RunDetail.tsx / RunReport.tsx to prefer the historical value over `checks.get(id)?.engine` once available.

## Found via

Multi-angle `/code-review` pass on PR #1551 (2026-08-28) — the altitude-angle finding recorded this as pre-existing/out-of-scope for a frontend badges PR rather than something to build inline.

=================== #2255
feat(privacy): a reason per entry in redacted_columns (own tag / inherited tag / policy / value classifier / default mask)
labels: enhancement,priority/P3  milestone: v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance
Split from #2114, which shipped the asset-level half: `inherited_classifications` on `GET /assets/{id}`, MCP `get_asset`, and a *Masked through lineage* panel on the asset page.

What remains is the per-result half. `redacted_columns` on run detail, MCP `get_run_results` and alerts says *that* a column was masked, not *why*. The decision is made per cell in `run_service._redact_row` / `_redact_comparison_row` through `_known_sensitive` / `_may_show_incidental`, which return a bool. Reporting a reason means those ladder functions return which rung decided (own tag, inherited tag, suite policy, value classifier, or the default mask for an unclassified incidental column), and `_RedactionTracker` keeps it per column.

This is a security-sensitive refactor of the redaction ladder, so it stays separate. It must not change what is masked: pin that with the existing redaction tests before touching the ladder.

## Data Quality Section Summary

**Rule attachment**
- **Property level:** Rules sit under a property's `quality:` key, e.g., under `properties:` → `- name: order_id` → `quality:`.
- **Schema object level:** Rules sit under a `schema:` object's `quality:` key. The page uses this for `rowCount` and multi-column duplicate checks.
- **Rule types:** The page lists four: `text`, `library`, `sql`, and `custom`.

**Library metrics**
- **`nullValues`** (property): counts nulls. Takes no arguments.
- **`missingValues`** (property): counts values treated as missing. Takes `arguments` → `missingValues`, an array such as null, empty strings, or "N/A".
- **`invalidValues`** (property): counts values failing a rule. Takes either `validValues` (an allowed-value array) or `pattern` (a regex).
- **`duplicateValues`**: at property level, counts duplicates in one column. At schema level, takes `arguments` → `properties`, a list of column names, to check compound uniqueness.
- **`rowCount`** (schema): counts rows in the table or object.
- **`unit`**: accepts `rows` or `percent`. The page says the default is rows in one example, though the field table doesn't state a default.
- **`type`**: can be omitted for library rules when `metric` is set.

**Operators**
- Single-value: `mustBe`, `mustNotBe`, `mustBeGreaterThan`, `mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo`, `mustBeLessThan`, `mustBeLessOrEqualTo`.
- Array-value: `mustBeBetween` and `mustNotBeBetween`. The page says `mustBeBetween` is equivalent to a greater-than lower bound plus a less-than upper bound.

**`sql` type**
- Uses `type: sql` and a `query` field containing a single query that returns a number or boolean. The query must match the target database's dialect.
- Placeholders `{object}` and `{property}` are replaced with the current table or view and column. Note that the page writes them without a `$` prefix. Its operator section also uses `{table}` and `{column}`, which is inconsistent with the placeholder definition.

**`custom` type**
- Uses `type: custom` with two key fields:
  - `engine`: any value is accepted, with common ones including soda, greatExpectations, and montecarlo.
  - `implementation`: a non-parsed text block passed through to the engine.
- The page gives Soda and Great Expectations examples.

**Example YAML**
- A `customer_id` property has a `nullValues` rule with `mustBe: 0` and a description.
- Other examples cover a percent-based `nullValues` check and a `rowCount` check at schema level.

- **`nullValues`** (property): counts nulls. Takes no arguments.
- **`missingValues`** (property): counts values treated as missing. Takes `arguments` → `missingValues`, an array such as null, empty strings, or "N/A".
- **`invalidValues`** (property): counts values failing a rule. Takes either `validValues` (an allowed-value array) or `pattern` (a regex).
- **`duplicateValues`**: at property level, counts duplicates in one column. At schema level, takes `arguments` → `properties`, a list of column names, to check compound uniqueness.
- **`rowCount`** (schema): counts rows in the table or object.
- **`unit`**: accepts `rows` or `percent`. The page says the default is rows in one example, though the field table doesn't state a default.
- **`type`**: can be omitted for library rules when `metric` is set.

**Operators**
- Single-value: `mustBe`, `mustNotBe`, `mustBeGreaterThan`, `mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo`, `mustBeLessThan`, `mustBeLessOrEqualTo`.
- Array-value: `mustBeBetween` and `mustNotBeBetween`. The page says `mustBeBetween` is equivalent to a greater-than lower bound plus a less-than upper bound.

**`sql` type**
- Uses `type: sql` and a `query` field containing a single query that returns a number or boolean. The query must match the target database's dialect.
- Placeholders `{object}` and `{property}` are replaced with the current table or view and column. Note that the page writes them without a `$` prefix. Its operator section also uses `{table}` and `{column}`, which is inconsistent with the placeholder definition.

**`custom` type**
- Uses `type: custom` with two key fields:
  - `engine`: any value is accepted, with common ones including soda, greatExpectations, and montecarlo.
  - `implementation`: a non-parsed text block passed through to the engine.
- The page gives Soda and Great Expectations examples.

**Example YAML**
- A `customer_id` property has a `nullValues` rule with `mustBe: 0` and a description.
- Other examples cover a percent-based `nullValues` check and a `rowCount` check at schema level.

## Object fields

Objects are tables, documents, or similar structures. Fields that apply to all elements are marked **(element)**.

- `id` (element)
- `name` (element, required)
- `physicalName` (element)
- `physicalType` (element): e.g., `table`, `view`, `topic`, `file`
- `logicalType` (element): typically `object` or `array`
- `businessName` (element)
- `description` (element)
- `deprecated` (element): defaults to `false`
- `synonyms` (element)
- `quality` (element)
- `tags` (element)
- `authoritativeDefinitions` (element)
- `customProperties` (element)
- `dataGranularityDescription`: object-only

## Property fields

Properties are attributes such as columns or payload fields.

- `id`, `name`, `physicalName`, `physicalType`, `logicalType`, `businessName`, `description`, `deprecated`, `synonyms`, `quality`, `tags`, `authoritativeDefinitions`, `customProperties` (inherited from elements)
- `logicalTypeOptions`: e.g., `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `format`
- `required`
- `unique`
- `primaryKey`
- `primaryKeyPosition`
- `partitioned`
- `partitionKeyPosition`
- `classification`
- `encryptedName`
- `criticalDataElement`
- `transformLogic`
- `transformDescription`
- `transformSourceObjects`
- `examples`
- `enum`
- `items` (for arrays)
- `map` (for maps)
- `semanticType`

This page does not define the internal structure of `quality` or `customProperties` entries, so they are left empty in the example below.

## Example YAML

```yaml
schema:
  - id: tbl_obj
    name: tbl
    physicalName: tbl_1
    physicalType: table
    logicalType: object
    businessName: Payment transactions
    description: Core payment metrics.
    dataGranularityDescription: Aggregated by txn_ref_dt and pmt_txn_id
    deprecated: false
    synonyms:
      - synonym: Payments
        locale: en-US
    authoritativeDefinitions:
      - url: https://catalog.example.com/datasets/payments
        type: businessDefinition
    tags: ['finance']
    quality: []
    customProperties: []
    properties:
      - id: txn_ref_dt_prop
        name: txn_ref_dt
        physicalName: txn_ref_dt
        physicalType: date
        logicalType: date
        businessName: Transaction reference date
        description: Date the transaction is referenced.
        logicalTypeOptions:
          format: "yyyy-MM-dd"
          minimum: "2000-01-01"
          maximum: "2030-12-31"
        required: true
        unique: false
        primaryKey: true
        primaryKeyPosition: 1
        partitioned: true
        partitionKeyPosition: 1
        classification: public
        criticalDataElement: false
        transformSourceObjects:
          - table_name_1
        transformLogic: "SELECT t1.txn_dt AS txn_ref_dt FROM table_name_1 AS t1"
        transformDescription: Takes the transaction date from the source table.
        examples:
          - "2024-07-10"
        tags: []
        customProperties: []

      - id: rcvr_id_prop
        name: rcvr_id
        physicalName: rcvr_id
        physicalType: varchar(18)
        logicalType: string
        businessName: Receiver ID
        description: Identifier of the payment receiver.
        logicalTypeOptions:
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 18
          pattern: "^[A-Z0-9]+$"
          format: "uuid"
        required: true
        unique: true
        primaryKey: false
        partitioned: false
        classification: restricted
        criticalDataElement: true
        encryptedName: rcvr_id_enc
        examples:
          - "RCV000123456789"
        tags: []
        customProperties: []

      - id: amount_prop
        name: amount
        physicalType: DECIMAL(12,2)
        logicalType: number
        description: Transaction amount.
        logicalTypeOptions:
          minimum: 0
          maximum: 1000000
        required: false
        unique: false
        classification: confidential
        criticalDataElement: false
        semanticType: measure
        transformLogic: "SUM(amount_local)"
```

## Environment
- conda env `dataq` — run python via `conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output ...` or `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/miniconda/base/envs/dataq/bin/python -m ...`.
- Postgres is the compose `postgres` service on localhost:5432 (being started by the orchestrator; wait until `docker compose ps postgres` in the MAIN repo dir shows healthy). Credentials are in the main repo's gitignored `.env` (`POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`). You have a DEDICATED test database named in your task brief — ALWAYS run pytest with `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg2://<user>:<pw>@localhost:5432/<your db>` (the conftest drop_alls the schema at teardown; sharing a DB with another agent breaks both). Do not source the whole `.env` (it exports WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS and breaks test_membership_service).
- Frontend: `cd frontend && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` first in a fresh worktree; `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm typecheck` (check package.json for exact names).
- Run full vitest and full pytest sequentially, never concurrently.

## Workflow (mandatory)
1. Branch from your worktree HEAD (it is `main`): `fix/issue-<N>-<slug>` or `feature/issue-<N>-<slug>`. Conventional commits; one functionality per commit; end commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
2. Tests for every behaviour change. For a bug/regression: prove the regression test FAILS against the unfixed code (revert the fix temporarily, run the test, restore) and say so in the PR body.
3. Local gate before push: `black --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy backend` (full sweep, not just your file), `bandit` as configured, pytest on your DB, and the frontend gate if you touched frontend. Pre-commit hooks must pass — never `--no-verify`.
4. Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/<PR-or-issue-number>.<section>.md` (see `changelog.d/README*` or existing fragments for sections). Use the issue number if the PR number is not known yet, then rename after opening the PR if the convention requires the PR number (check scripts/changelog.py).
5. Docs: update `docs/site/` pages the change touches (and CLAUDE.md only if a standing rule changes). Tick the item in `docs/progress.md` Week 5 table: `⬜` → `✅` with `— [PR #N](...)`.
6. Push and open the PR with `gh pr create` (body: what/why, tests, the "proved the test fails" note, `Fixes #N`), set milestone `v1.3 Week 5 — integrations & governance` (`gh pr edit --milestone`). End the PR body with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
7. Run the code review skill on the PR: invoke `Skill` with skill `code-review` and args `<PR number> --comment` (level: medium). Fix every finding in the same PR with follow-up `fixup:`-style commits (plain push, never force-push). Anything you deliberately defer: file a GitHub issue with labels + milestone (`gh issue create`) and reference it in the PR. Never silently drop a finding; "pre-existing" is not a disposition.
8. Wait for CI (`gh pr checks <N> --watch`). If red, fix. Resolve review threads (unresolved threads block merge on this repo). DO NOT MERGE — the orchestrator merges. Report back: PR number, CI state, findings fixed/filed, anything you could not do.

## Guardrails
- No credentials in tracked files. No new dependencies without checking license (rule 40). No Azure-specific logic.
- Redaction of PII happens at the logger and in run_service's ladder — never widen what is shown.
- MCP tools: docstrings are LLM-facing; state blind spots as fields, not prose; re-read sibling tool docstrings that your change may make false.
- Migrations: additive only; generate a fresh revision id and check it does not collide; `down_revision` must be the CURRENT head (`alembic heads`); test up AND down.

# ADR 0051 — Suite-on-suite triggers: a suite's own success as a trigger provider

- **Status:** Accepted (2026-10-25)
- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) (the `OrchestrationProvider` contract), [0011](0011-extensibility-seams-for-deferred-integrations.md) (`trigger_bindings` as the provider-agnostic trigger key), [0029](0029-dbt-orchestration-provider.md) (the last time the provider value-set widened), [0046](0046-pipeline-dq-gate.md) (the gate, which this does **not** extend), [0027](0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) (per-suite `view`/`edit`).

## Context

A suite runs today on a schedule, by hand, or when a bound **orchestration** pipeline or DAG
succeeds. The long-deferred ask is the fourth source: run suite B when suite A has run and passed —
a downstream dataset's checks only make sense once the upstream dataset has been verified, and
two suites bound to the same pipeline run in parallel, not in order.

The reason it was deferred stands: DataQ is not an orchestrator. Sequencing work is the
orchestrator's job (CLAUDE.md §4), and a suite that fans out into a graph of suites is a
mini-DAG DataQ would then have to schedule, retry and visualise. The customer's orchestrator
already does all of that. What it cannot do is express "when **DataQ** says the upstream is
good"; the gate (ADR 0046) covers that for a pipeline stage, but not for a suite that has no
pipeline of its own — a suite on a flat-file landing zone, a reconciliation suite that should
follow the two suites it reconciles.

`trigger_bindings` is `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env) → suite_id` and is already
provider-agnostic; the only provider-specific part of a trigger is who **observes** the
completion. For an orchestrator that is a webhook or a poll; for a suite it is DataQ itself,
at the moment the run reaches its terminal state. Nothing else in the chain —
`insert_triggered_run`, the `triggered_by` marker, the dedup index, dispatch — cares where the
event came from.

## Decision

1. **A suite is a trigger provider, not an orchestration provider.** `provider = 'suite'`
   joins a new `TRIGGER_PROVIDERS` value-set (`adf`, `airflow`, `dbt`, `suite`) that governs
   `trigger_bindings.provider`, binding validation and the `triggered_by` dedup predicate.
   `ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS` is **unchanged**: there is no `suite` connection type, no
   `pipeline_runs` row, no poller, no webhook, no health signal, and the gate endpoint
   (ADR 0046) refuses `provider='suite'` — a suite chain has no pipeline stage to answer.
2. **The binding key.** `pipeline_or_dag_id` holds the **upstream suite's id**; `env` must
   equal the upstream suite's connection env and is filled in by the server, so the firing
   lookup stays the one every provider uses: `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env, enabled)`.
3. **When it fires: success only, by default and for now.** A run fires its bindings when it
   reaches `succeeded` with no check at `fail` or `critical` (a `warn` passes, an `error`ed or
   skipped check does not block — the run still verified what it could). A run that `failed`,
   was `cancelled`, or has a breach fires nothing; the downstream suite is not run against
   data the upstream just said was bad. A per-binding `fire_on` predicate is deliberately not
   added until someone asks for it with a case: the "run B on A's failure" shape is an alert,
   which notifications already deliver.
4. **The marker.** The downstream run carries `triggered_by = 'suite:<upstream_suite_id>:<upstream_run_id>'`.
   Both ids are UUIDs, so unlike every orchestrator marker this one **can** be split — but
   readers still go through `orchestration.markers`, and the partial unique index
   `uq_runs_suite_triggered_by` (predicate widened to `suite:%`) makes a re-fired completion
   (a worker retry, a reaper flipping a stuck run) a no-op, exactly as for pipeline events.
5. **Guards, at authoring and at firing.**
   - *Self:* a suite cannot be bound to itself (422).
   - *Cycle:* creating a binding that would make the upstream reachable from the downstream
     through enabled **or disabled** suite bindings is refused (422, naming the path). Disabled
     ones count because `enabled` is a toggle, not a deletion, and re-enabling must not be the
     moment a cycle appears.
   - *Depth:* at firing time a chain deeper than `SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH` (5) stops and logs
     `suite_trigger_depth_exceeded` instead of running — the depth is read back through the
1:# ADR 0014 — Cross-dataset reconciliation as a `comparison` check kind (reuse FastAPI_DataComparison engine)

17:2. **Only FDC's engine is reusable; its app is not.** FDC's connection store (SQLite `connections.db`, passwords hex-encoded plaintext), auth (bearer token, local-only `127.0.0.1`), UI (Jinja templates), and result storage (disk files) all conflict with DataQ's hardened equivalents (Postgres, `SecretStore`/Key Vault, Azure AD, React, `results` table). The pure diff engine — `data_comparison/{column_comparison,record_comparison,get_dataset}.py` — is the part worth porting.
19:3. **A comparison check references *two* connections** (source + target), which breaks DataQ's invariant that a check/suite binds to **one** connection. This is the one genuine design decision and is deferred to a future ADR (see Decision §5).

# changelog.d — one file per change

Every PR that changes something a user, deployer or API client would notice adds **one
small file here** instead of editing `docs/site/reference/changelog.md`. The published
page renders these under **Unreleased** at build time; at release
`scripts/changelog.py assemble` moves them into a dated section and deletes them.

## Filename

```
<number>.<section>.md         e.g. 2395.changed.md
<number>-<n>.<section>.md     a second entry for the same number, e.g. 2440-2.added.md
```

- `<number>` — the issue the change belongs to (the PR number if there is no issue).
- `<n>` — `2`, `3`, … for further fragments of the same number.
- `<section>` — `breaking` | `security` | `added` | `changed` | `fixed`.

Only files matching this grammar (plus this README) may live here.

## Body

The bullet's text in Markdown, **without** the leading `- `, continuation lines unindented.
Lead with a bold phrase, as the existing entries do, and describe the behaviour — never cite
an issue or PR number, the page is public (CONTRIBUTING rule 41).

```markdown
**Changelog entries are collected one file per change.** A PR adds a fragment under
`changelog.d/` and the published page assembles them, so two PRs never conflict on the
changelog.
```

## Commands

```bash
python scripts/changelog.py lint                 # every fragment is well-formed (pre-commit + CI)
python scripts/changelog.py render-unreleased    # preview the Unreleased section
python scripts/changelog.py check --base origin/main   # what CI asks of a PR
python scripts/changelog.py assemble --version 1.3.0 --date 2026-11-29   # at release
```
